eyebrow: Quantum Programming with Q# & Azure Quantum · Chapter 1
titlePlain: What Q# Is & When to Reach for
subtitle: Lesson 1 · Q# Language Fundamentals

steps.label: Qiskit is a Python SDK
steps.sub: QuantumCircuit and Aer are ordinary Python classes bolted onto the language

steps.label: Q# is its own compiled language
steps.sub: Own grammar, own type checker, own compiler — the QDK

steps.label: A .qs file is a different file type
steps.sub: Not Python with quantum decorations, the way .rs isn't Python with Rust decorations

steps.label: Operations are first-class
steps.sub: A declared, typed construct the compiler enforces like any function

steps.label: Static typing catches mistakes early
steps.sub: Wrong return type or wrong qubit count fails before anything touches hardware

steps.label: Controlled and Adjoint are compiler-derived
steps.sub: The controlled or inverse version of your operation is generated automatically

steps.label: No equivalent in Qiskit
steps.sub: You'd build the controlled or inverse circuit yourself, gate by gate

steps.label: Answers a different question
steps.sub: Not "what's the output today" but "how many qubits and how long on future fault-tolerant hardware"

steps.label: No execution required
steps.sub: Not on real hardware, not even on a simulator — just the operation and a hardware profile

steps.label: First-class in the Q# stack
steps.sub: Nothing comparable ships as a core feature of Qiskit

steps.label: Python/ML pipeline integration
steps.sub: Qiskit's Python-native ecosystem — no serialization boundary to cross

steps.label: Hardware proposals and qubit-count estimates
steps.sub: Q# and Azure Quantum's resource estimator is the tool built for exactly that

steps.label: Not mutually exclusive
steps.sub: The qsharp Python package bridges both worlds later in this course

subtitle: The two real ways to write and run Q# today, and installing the modern QDK.
